key_insight: Neural Fourier Surrogates (NFS) provide a classical stochastic baseline that learns the same finite Fourier support as data-reuploading QNNs, enabling a more direct comparison of quantum and classical expressivity.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML practitioners, NFS offers a practical benchmark to test whether QNN gains come from quantum effects or from Fourier-spectrum capacity that can be matched classically.
method: Uses a stochastic neural architecture to estimate coefficients over a finite Fourier series support.
Draws inspiration from Neural Quantum States and Random Fourier Features.
Compares learned Fourier spectra of QNNs and NFS on synthetic data.
evidence_signal: On tabular benchmark datasets, NFS is reported to be broadly competitive with standard classical baselines and comparable to data-reuploading QNNs.
watch_item: Because NFS is a surrogate baseline rather than a quantum model, parity in performance does not by itself demonstrate quantum advantage or absence of hardware-related constraints.
paper_title: Neural Fourier Surrogates for Data Reuploading Quantum Neural Networks
